neighbours.label: context of classic early science fiction (Wells, Verne, Swift, Poe): fires on function words and punctuation in such text
fire: The Time Machine by H. G. Wells and the novels of Jules Verne founded science fiction.
Science fiction elements appear in the stories of Edgar Allan Poe.
Jules Verne is considered, along with H. G. Wells, a father of science fiction.
The War of the Worlds and The Island of Doctor Moreau were written by Wells.
Jonathan Swift, in Gulliver's Travels, imagined a flying island.
Herbert George Wells was born in Bromley, Kent, in 1866.
Verne wrote Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea and Journey to the Centre of the Earth.
In New Atlantis, Francis Bacon imagined a society built on science.
quiet: Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen and the novels of Charles Dickens shaped the Victorian novel.
Gothic elements appear in the stories of the Brontë sisters.
Charles Dickens is considered, along with George Eliot, a master of the Victorian novel.
Great Expectations and Bleak House were written by Dickens.
Jane Austen, in Emma, described a matchmaking heroine.
Thomas Hardy was born in Dorset, England, in 1840.
Tolstoy wrote War and Peace and Anna Karenina.
In Middlemarch, George Eliot portrayed a provincial town.
